lines.text: This killer whale just dropped a fish on purpose, and it is not a mistake.
It happened at Marineland, a park in Canada where orcas live in captivity, and a scientist spotted it by accident while recording their calls.
A young male would spit up a fish onto the surface, then sink down and wait.
Soon a hungry seagull spotted the free snack and landed on the water.
And the whale shot up from below with its mouth wide open.
He did this again and again. It was a trap.
Here's the twist. A few months later, his little half brother started doing it too.
Then adult females joined in, until several whales at the park were baiting gulls.
The scientist said it was like watching a tradition being born.
Some scientists are not sure whether the whales copied each other or each worked it out alone.
So did that young whale invent the trick all by himself? What do you think?
